items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Terminology 18:1
items.html: (To the question) What is the protrusion of light in the back of the head? It was explained above in Answer 15, that from Aba and Ima and below there is no aspect of AB from the Hochma of the direct light, but from the Hochma of the thirty-two paths, which is only the Bina of the direct light that returns to Hochma, see there. Therefore in these Mochin there are only three aspects: one, the Bina that returned to Hochma, which is the GAR of the Mochin; two, the aspect of the Tifferet, which is the bearer of the illumination of Hochma; three, the Yesod, which is the aspect of the Nukva of these Mochin, which is the bearer of the aspect of the screens that raise the returning light to clothe the direct light, as is known. And corresponding to the three aspects in the Mochin, three Partzufim came out: Aba and Ima, ZA, and the Nukva, and through the flashing of the Mochin outward (see Answer 41 below) three protrusions come out. One on the forehead of Aba and Ima, which are the aspect of the GAR of these Mochin that protrude there. The second is on the forehead of ZA, where the aspect of the Tifferet of the Mochin protrudes, which is the aspect of the bearer of the illumination of Hochma. And these two protrusions are in the aspect of the face, namely on the forehead, being the aspect of the direct light of the Mochin. And the third protrusion, which is the aspect of the screens of the Mochin, its beginning of coming out is in the back of the head of ZA, being an aspect of returning light alone, which is an aspect of back and not face. And this protrusion is called the knot of the Tefillin, and it is the aspect of the root Makif of the Nukva. See above, Answer 7. However, its main place is on the forehead of the Nukva, in the secret of the Tefillin of the hand. As is said below in Answer 43. (Item 158).
